data.name: Ghaazi
data.gender_notes: Ghaazi is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Someone who gains a victory, a warrior or a fighter. The name Ghaazi carries the meaning “Conqueror, Victor” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Ghaazi usually hope their child will grow to embody conqueror, victor and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A person who strives for spiritual victory and conquers his inner demons
data.etymology: Ghaazi belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Conqueror, Victor.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ghaazi total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_arabic.name: غازي
in_arabic.meaning: من يقاتل في سبيل الله، المجاهد في الحرب
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم غازي مشتق من الفعل غازى، وهو من الجذور العربية التي تعني القتال في سبيل الله أو المجاداة في الحرب. يدل على الشجاعة والبسالة في مواجهة الأعداء، وغالبًا ما يوصف به المجاهدون والشهداء في المعارك دفاعًا عن الدين أو الأراضي الإسلامية. استخدم هذا الاسم تاريخيًا لوصف القادة العسكريين والأنصار الذين يقاتلون بضراوة في المعارك.

in_urdu.name: غازي
in_urdu.meaning: اللہ کی راہ میں لڑنے والا، جنگ میں بہادر
in_urdu.long_meaning: نام غازی عربی زبان کے الفعل غازى سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے اللہ کی راہ میں لڑنا یا جنگ میں شجاعت دکھانا۔ یہ نام اسلامی ثقافت میں ان بہادروں کے لئے استعمال ہوتا ہے جو دین کی حفاظت کے لئے لڑتے ہیں۔ تاریخی طور پر، غازی کا لقب ان بہادروں کو دیا جاتا تھا جنہوں نے دشمنوں کے خلاف اسلامی ریاستوں کا دفاع کیا، اور یہ ان کی شجاعت اور نڈرता کا ایک اعزاز سمجھا جاتا تھا۔

in_hindi.name: ग़ाज़ी
in_hindi.meaning: भगवान की लड़ाई लड़ने वाला, युद्ध में बहादुर
in_hindi.long_meaning: नाम ग़ाज़ी अरबी भाषा के क्रिया ग़ाज़ी से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है भगवान की लड़ाई लड़ना या युद्ध में वीरता दिखाना। यह नाम उन बहादुरों के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है जो धार्मिक रक्षा के लिए युद्ध में जाते हैं। ऐतिहासिक रूप से, ग़ाज़ी की उपाधि उन वीर सैनिकों को दी जाती थी जिन्होंने दुश्मनों के खिलाफ इस्लामी क्षेत्रों का बचाव किया, और यह उनकी बहादुरी और निडरता का प्रतीक माना जाता था।

in_pashto.name: غازی
in_pashto.meaning: د الله په لاره کې جنګیالی، په جګړه کې ښه سړی
in_pashto.long_meaning: د غازی نوم د عربي ژبې د فعل غازي څخه اخیستل شوی دی، چې معنی یې د الله په لاره کې جنګیدل یا په جګړه کې ښه والی ښودل دي. دا نوم د هغو کسانو لپاره کارول کیږي چې د دین د ساتنې لپاره جنګیږي. تاریخي پلوه، غازی لقب هغو کسانو ته ورکړل شوی دی چې د دښمنانو پر وړاندې يې د اسلامي دولتونو دفاع کوله، او دا د هغوی د شجاعت او نړیتوب یو اعزاز ګڼل کیده.

in_english.name: Ghaazi
in_english.meaning: One who fights in the way of Allah, warrior in battle
in_english.long_meaning: The name Ghaazi originates from the Arabic root 'غ ز ي' (gha-zā-y), which means to fight or struggle, particularly in the cause of Allah. It refers to a warrior, a champion, or a hero who engages in battle, especially for the sake of defending Islam or Muslim territories. Historically, the term 'Ghaazi' was used to describe military leaders and soldiers who fought bravely in defense of their faith and lands. The name symbolizes courage, valor, and dedication to the cause of jihad, which holds significant spiritual and cultural importance in Islamic tradition.

data.cultural_impact: The term "Ghaazi" holds a deep cultural significance in Islamic history. Historically, it refers to someone who gains a victory against the enemy, particularly in a religious war or jihad. A Ghaazi is a warrior or a fighter, who dedicates their life to protect their community, culture, and faith. The devotion and bravery of Ghaazis have been celebrated in Islamic poetry and literature, and their legacies continue to inspire generations.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name "Ghaazi" lies in its reminder of the importance of self-sacrifice and bravery in the quest for a noble cause. The journey of a Ghaazi is an embodiment of the Islamic concept of submission (Islam means submission to God in Arabic), where one dedicates their life to a greater purpose and strives for personal and moral growth in the pursuit of a righteous cause. The name symbolizes a warrior of faith, who stands up against injustice and fights for the protection of their community, their culture, and their faith in a courageous and selfless manner.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Conqueror, Victor" symbolizes Someone who gains a victory, a warrior or a fighter. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Ghaazi serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of conqueror, victor.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Al-Ghazali, a prominent scholar and theologian in Islamic history, is named as 'Al-Ghazi' due to his military campaigns against the Crusaders in the Middle East. He led several raids against the Crusader states in the late 11th and early 12th centuries, and his military exploits earned him the title 'Al-Ghazi' or 'the warrior'.
historical_references.context: Islamic military campaigns against the Crusaders in the Middle East

historical_references.reference: Salah ad-Din Yusuf ibn Ayyub, commonly known as Saladin, is another famous Islamic figure who is referred to as 'Al-Ghazi'. He was the founder and first sultan of the Ayyubid dynasty in Egypt and Syria. Saladin led several successful military campaigns against the Crusaders and the Zengids, and he retook Jerusalem from the Crusaders in 1187. The title 'Al-Ghazi' further emphasized his military prowess and his role in defending Islamic lands from foreign invasions.
historical_references.context: Islamic military campaigns against the Crusaders and the Zengids
